title: Air-fryer chorizo
subtitle: Sliced cooking chorizo crisped quickly in the air fryer.
excerpt: Slices of Spanish cooking chorizo air-fried until the edges caramelise and the fat renders into the flesh. Use in pasta, rice dishes, or alongside fried eggs. Serves four as a component.
sourceNotes: Cooking chorizo is a fresh or semi-cured sausage from Spain and Portugal flavoured with pimentón (smoked paprika). It is used across Spanish and Portuguese cooking as a flavouring ingredient. This air-fryer preparation crisps the slices for use as a topping or component.

content.text: Chorizo needs no added oil in the air fryer: it renders its own fat as it cooks. Slice about 1 cm thick and lay in a single layer. The edges caramelise in 6-8 minutes at 190°C. Use the crisped slices over pasta, stirred into rice, or alongside fried eggs.

Lay {{chorizo}} of sliced chorizo in a single layer in the air fryer basket. No oil needed. Cook at 190°C for 4 minutes, flip each slice, and cook for a further 3-4 minutes until the edges are caramelised and the fat has rendered. Tip onto a plate lined with paper towel to absorb any excess fat.

items.cause: Rendered fat dripping into the hot pan.
items.fix: Add a small amount of water to the drip tray before cooking to prevent the fat from smoking. Empty and wipe after each batch.
Cook at 190°C rather than 200°C. Chorizo has sugars from the paprika that burn quickly at high heat.
Aim for 1 cm slices. Thinner slices curl away from the basket and cook unevenly.

content.text: Crisped chorizo is a useful component. Add it to pasta with tinned tomatoes and basil, stir it through rice with peas, or pile it on toast with soft-boiled eggs. The rendered fat that collects in the drip tray can be poured into a small jar and used to fry eggs or potatoes.
